subject: Drop one marker at a time

messages.author: 6f2103452e93a49d
messages.subject: Drop one marker at a time
parts:
Hi Dr. Broman, 

Finally I got one map but there were two big gaps on two chromosome separately. I used "droponemarker" on a chromosome and got the image as attached.  I don't know how to interpret this result. In the bottom panel, there is a gap,range from 100cM to 200cM, which is similar as the gap size on the map. 
Dose it mean that if I drop one this suspicious marker, the chromosome length would decrease ~100cM? 

Thanks for your time and patience. I really appreciate! 


1.       dropone<- droponemarker(KNC_1, chr=10, error.prob=0.0001, map.function=”kosambi”, maxit=1000, sex.sp=FALSE)

par(mfrow=c(2,1))

 plot(dropone, lod=1, ylim=c(-100,0))

 plot(dropone, lod=2, ylab="Change in chromosome length")

summary(dropone, lod.column=2)

                   chr pos  LOD Ldiff

SNP_05134  10 464 4.53  20.8



Best, 

Chen

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Drop one marker at a time
parts:
The figure showed up as a big black square.

But yes, I think it should be that if you drop that marker, the chromosome length will go down by ~100 cM.
Try dropping it and see what happens.

karl
